source_metadata.question:
Three circles with radius 2 are drawn in such a way that each time one of the points of intersection of two circles is identical with the centre of the third circle. How big is the area of the grey zone?

target.visual_information: A curved overlap region formed by intersecting circular outlines. On the left, use the tan lens labeled 79 inside both product-preference circles. On the right, use one of the gray curved components between the white central overlap and a pair of outer arcs.
target.left_evidence: The tan lens labeled 79 inside both product-preference circles.
target.right_evidence: One of the gray curved components between the white central overlap and a pair of outer arcs.
target.left_meaning: The lens represents customers who prefer both product categories.
target.right_meaning: The gray components consist of locations inside exactly two of the three circles. The center common to all three is unshaded.
target.reason: The left lens encodes joint membership in two named sets. The right gray region selects pieces of a geometric area by circle coverage.
target.reasoning_consequence: Correctly interpreting the markings means using 79 for the both-categories count on the left and excluding the white triple overlap when finding the shaded area on the right.
